validation: Positive borrowing is a deficit; negative borrowing is a surplus.
Total managed expenditure − current receipts = net borrowing (all excluding public sector banks).
Total managed expenditure = current expenditure + consumption of fixed capital + net investment.
Selected tax details cover central government and do not form an exhaustive public-sector receipts decomposition.
Debt/GDP is the published ONS ratio; optional flow/GDP scaling is calculated by the dashboard using separately sourced nominal GDP.
All historical observations use this release vintage and are subject to revision.

sources.history: 2003-04 to 2025-26 in tables 4.2/4.4; detailed table 5.2 covers 2021-22 to 2025-26. Single publication vintage with explicit classification breaks.
sources.discovery: Pinned PESA 2026 edition. Review newer PESA editions annually; do not silently change classification.
sources.historyUnits: Table 4.2 £ billion converted to £ million; table 4.4 published % of GDP (ONS GDP vintage 30 June 2026).
historyValidation: Eleven function totals reconcile to TES within source rounding; keep explicit rounding adjustment.
TES plus published accounting adjustments bridges to TME within source rounding.
Debt interest is an of-which part of general public services, not an additional function.
Retain education/student loans (2011-12), transport/TfL (2011-12), Network Rail (2015-16) and EU transactions (2010-11) classification notes.

sources.basis: Latest available four-quarter nominal GDP, current prices, not seasonally adjusted. Dashboard scaling, not an official ONS fiscal ratio.
validation: Sum four consecutive published BKTL quarters. No interpolation, forecast or inference from rounded debt/GDP ratios.
Scale flows by the latest quarter-end denominator at or before the flow endpoint, with at most two months of carry-forward; otherwise unavailable.
Monthly and year-to-date flows are shares of annual GDP, without annualising the numerator.
Historical GDP is the latest release vintage and may differ from the vintage underlying published fiscal ratios.
